editorial:
Imagine waking up in a world where science and religion crash into each other in the weirdest way possible. You are thrown into a dark, gritty setting where a strange group of people are trying to push the limits of life and death. The vibe is very moody and a bit creepy, making you feel like something is always hiding just out of sight. It feels like a fever dream where you are not quite sure if what you are seeing is real or just a nightmare. The characters are desperate and pushed to the edge, which keeps you wondering who is actually in control of the situation.

What really pops is the strange imagery and the way the tension builds up slowly. The acting is raw, though some parts of the story might feel a bit confusing since it does not hold your hand. If you love weird indie films that take big risks, you will dig this. It is a wild ride that is definitely for the brave.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head when the main character realizes that the experiments were never about saving people. The big twist is that the process actually creates a cycle of pain and rebirth that cannot be stopped. In the final scenes, the characters face a scary version of themselves. It ends on a dark note where you realize that the quest for eternal life only brought more suffering and a total loss of humanity.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves strange indie horror and sci-fi mixes.
